findings.reason: the population is the gate's denominator, so a regression the resolver change causes in routing, gc or interface_counts tests would pass the node unmeasured, which is the same omission the population was widened to fix.
findings.text: the population claims to cover "any module that calls `_resolve_commit`" but its parenthetical list omits three direct callers: `reckon/crew/routing.py` (lines 763, 2295), `reckon/crew/gc.py` (line 473) and `reckon/interface_counts.py` (line 685, excluded by the "(all under `reckon/crew/`)" clause), while it names two modules that only re-export the function without calling it (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:267`, `reckon/crew/promotion.py:102`) — and since §64's deliverable changes `_resolve_commit`'s contract so an instrument fault is no longer an empty-string answer, those three unlisted callers are exactly the sites whose behaviour the change can break

findings.reason: a worker implementing only the four-commit cases can leave the single-cited-commit hole open and still pass the gate, so the measure does not cover the rule the deliverable states.
findings.text: the deliverable at plan.html:1332 requires refusal "where a cited commit cannot be resolved while the revision is chosen", but every asserted case cites four commits and exercises only `_descendant_commit`'s multi-entry branch; the `len(entries) == 1` shortcut at promotion_scope.py:352 returns the presented text unconditionally, so a run citing a single commit that fails to resolve at selection time is still recorded as its promoted revision and no declared case or negative control fails

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_resolve_commit` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:201), `_descendant_commit` (reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:317), `_resolve_commits` (promotion_scope.py:266), `_revision_is_ancestor` (promotion_scope.py:2416), `promotion_checks.py` landing resolution (promotion_checks.py:981), `reports._commit_resolves_in` (reports.py:2093), `_commit_canonical_id` (promotion_evidence.py:366), `_land_a_promoted_run` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2614), `select_review_for_head` (recovery_review_subject.py:111), `tests/test_one_function_resolves_a_citation.py` and `tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py` all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the no-added-failure population at plan.html:1344 enumerates modules that call `_resolve_commit` and omits three real direct callers (`reckon/crew/routing.py`, `reckon/crew/gc.py`, `reckon/interface_counts.py`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — arms come from git checkouts under the run's own scratch directory, every gate log sits under the run directory, and the manifest carries flat `baseline_suite`/`after_suite` records.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test name `tests/test_a_commit_that_fails_to_resolve_refuses_the_promotion.py` states the mechanism, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the cited code matches the stated root cause (`_descendant_commit` keeps an unresolved entry out of `resolvable` at promotion_scope.py:340-357, and `_resolve_commit` returns `""` for both a non-commit and a `timeout=10`/`OSError` at recovery_review_subject.py:214-231), the mechanism (refuse on an unresolvable cited commit, raise an instrument fault) produces the done-when, and it runs on the real path `promotion_release._run_promoted_revision` → `promotion_scope._promoted_revision` → `_descendant_commit`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §64 delivers one thing (the promotion refuses instead of dropping an unresolved cited commit); the land's own head check is split out to §65.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §64 is carried by the open followup `f-crpc-s64-s65` (plan.html:1600-1603) whose prompt names `/reckon-build crew-runtime-positive-controls §64`, `plan-section-depends-on` declares `{"s64":[]}` and the section relies only on already-done §63.
